 ORDER
The learned High Court Government Pleader accepts notice for the respondent No.1.

2. Sri Prasantha V G, learned counsel files vakalath on behalf of the respondent No.2.
3.

The respondent No.2 lodged the FIR alleging that the petitioner No.1 who was a former employee of the company was appointed to the post of Senior-Director-Cloud & Data Centre Ops under the terms of the offer letter dated 11.12.2020, and his employment commenced with effect from 15.2.2021.

During his employment, an internal complaint was NC: 2023:KHC:41225 raised against him alleging that the petitioner No.1 had fraudulently on boarded an entity by the name SDX Hive Software Services as a vendor of the company and had thereafter approved payments to SDX Hive Software Services without the company having received any services from it in exchange.

sentences.text: It is further alleged that the petitioners have fraudulently and dishonestly induced the company to transfer monies to SDX Hive Software Services for services/deliverables that were never given to the company.
The police registered the FIR for the offences punishable under Sections 120B, 406, 408, 420 and 468 of IPC.
4. The parties are present before this Court.
5. The petitioners have annexed the copy of settlement agreement between the petitioners and the company of which the respondent No.2 is the Authorized Officer.
A perusal of the agreement indicated that the parties have amicably resolved the dispute among themselves.
In terms of the settlement, the petitioners have paid a sum of Rs.3,50,00,000/- to the company of which the respondent No.2 is the Authorized Officer, towards full and final settlement of the claim.
The respondent No.2 has agreed to withdraw all the allegations against the petitioners.

6. Though the offences are cognizable and non- compoundable, however, having regard to the fact that, the NC: 2023:KHC:41225 parties have amicably resolved the dispute among themselves, and the respondent No.2 having agreed to withdraw all the allegations made against the petitioners, it would be a futile exercise if the petitioners - accused are subjected to investigation, since the probability of police filing charge sheet is remote and bleak in view of the settlement.
Therefore, the continuation of criminal proceedings will be an abuse of the process of law.

Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER i) Criminal petition is allowed.
ii) The impugned FIR in Crime No.420/2023 registered by the Mahadevapura Police,
Bengaluru is hereby quashed.
iii) The Investigating Officer is directed to defreeze the bank account of the petitioner No.1 forthwith.
